parsed.explanation: Parent regime creates border and facilities exposure: visa officers may refuse on document/sex discrepancy with a possible fraud/ineligibility finding, passports are reported confiscated, and many subnational bans apply. This division adds a harsher layer: from 1 July 2026 using a restroom/changing room inconsistent with birth sex is a crime in government and public-facing private businesses including hospitals, punishable by up to one year, the only such private-business law described. That is a tier-1 universal exposure a visitor cannot pass or negotiate, with custody reported elsewhere in men's facilities after a bathroom arrest. Courts and a pre-effective-date suit show contestation, but no outcome, narrowing remaining in force, or enforcement history is documented, and functioning courts do not mitigate until shown to block the law. No organised sweeps, extortion, or executions are documented, keeping this above the 0.25 tier.
